note: Who a reveal is for (AUD-2, ED-10): the whole table, or one participant by id. An audience is an identity, never a credential and never an alias (AUD-11). Nothing here ties an audience to a document type — AUD-9 is a service rule, not a schema shape (ED-14) — so lifting it later changes no slot, mask or eligibility row. On the GM channel a slot is named by its audience; a table client is never told one (SEC-15).

invalid.name: a participant named by alias
invalid.why: AUD-11: an alias is a display name, never an identifier, and never leaves the GM's channel

invalid.name: a participant with no id
invalid.why: ED-10: a participant audience is an identity; there is nothing to evaluate without one

invalid.name: the table audience carrying a participant id
invalid.why: the table is not a participant; one shape per audience, and no half-named slot

invalid.name: a bare string
invalid.why: an audience is a discriminated object, so a second kind cannot be added by string

invalid.name: an audience kind this contract does not define
invalid.why: closed vocabulary: a group audience is an amendment with a device-approval story (ED-14), not a value

invalid.name: a participant id outside the id alphabet
